methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in AI & Software (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in AI & Software, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Eon Systems operates in the AI & Software sector at an undisclosed stage. The broader peer universe comprises 12 same-sector companies: one public comparable (Palantir; ticker PLTR) and eight private firms including Palantir, Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition. However, no sufficiently narrow peer subset exists to support a conventional peer-median valuation. Filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparables yielded fewer than three datapoints, making a tight peer-median approach inapplicable.

The peer-median method was therefore not pursued, as falling back to an all-sector median across 12 heterogeneous AI & Software companies would introduce uncontrolled dispersion and obscure stage-specific and tier-specific pricing dynamics. The single public comparable (PLTR) and the identified private peers represent a broad landscape but lack the granularity required for a robust triangulation anchored to peer multiples.

Without sufficient narrow-set comps, a defensible valuation range cannot be derived from the data provided. Key uncertainties include Eon Systems' precise funding stage, prior valuation, and revenue scale—all undisclosed. A complete valuation would require either disclosure of these parameters to enable narrower peer filtering, or application of alternative methods (scenario analysis, DCF) supported by operational and financial data not currently available.
